Write a raster to one file

Source: R/write.R
write_raster_file.Rd

Writes a raster to one file at a given path: one layer, or several layers as the bands of one file. Use it to save a raster made or changed in R, or to copy a raster file to another path or data type. Without datatype, the data type is the one stored with x's file, or, for a raster held in memory, the smallest type that holds its values. To write one file per layer in a folder, use write_rasters().

Usage

write_raster_file(
  x,
  filename,
  datatype = NULL,
  round_int = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

The raster to write: a SpatRaster with one or more layers, or a path to a raster file. Several layers are written as the bands of the one file, in layer order, each band named after its layer.

filename

The file to write: a single path. Its extension sets the format (GeoTIFF for .tif). Its parent folder is created, with any missing parents, if it does not exist.

datatype

The data type of the file, one of terra's types: "INT1U", "INT2U", "INT2S", "INT4U", "INT4S", "INT8U", "INT8S", "FLT4S" or "FLT8S". NULL (the default) takes it from x: the data type stored with its file, if every layer has one and they are the same; otherwise (a layer is held in memory, such as one made or changed in R, or the layers' stored types differ) the type inferred from the values, with a message naming it (see Method).

round_int

A single logical. TRUE (the default) rounds values to the nearest whole number, halves away from zero, before writing them as an integer type ("INT..."); FALSE writes them as they are, so the decimals are cut off (towards zero). Values written as a float type ("FLT4S", "FLT8S") are never rounded, whatever round_int is.

overwrite

A single logical: TRUE (the default) replaces an existing filename; FALSE stops with an error, before anything is written, if it exists.

Value

filename, invisibly.

Method

  • File: x is written with terra::writeRaster() to filename, in the format its extension sets (a GeoTIFF for .tif). Several layers become bands in layer order, each band named after its layer. Cells, extent, resolution and CRS are written as they are: no resampling or reprojection.

  • Data type: datatype, if given. With NULL, the type stored with x's file (terra::datatype()) if every layer has one and they are all the same. Otherwise it is inferred from the values of all layers, which are all read (in blocks, for a large raster held in a file): if every value that is not NA is a whole number, the smallest integer type that holds their range without using its NoData value, unsigned when the smallest value is 0 or more ("INT1U" for 0 to 254, "INT2U" for 0 to 65,534, "INT4U" for 0 to 4,294,967,294; "INT2S" for -32,767 to 32,767, "INT4S" for -2,147,483,647 to 2,147,483,647); otherwise, or if the range needs more than 32 bits, "FLT4S" when every value is within "FLT4S"'s range (about +/-3.4e38) and "FLT8S" beyond it. A raster whose values are all NA gets "INT1U". A message (cli::cli_inform()) names the type chosen and why; give datatype to choose another. The type is decided from x as given, before rounding.

  • Rounding: with round_int = TRUE and an integer data type, values are first rounded to the nearest whole number, halves away from zero (terra::round(): 0.5 becomes 1, -1.5 becomes -2, 0.75 becomes 1), because terra cuts decimals off when it writes them as integers (0.75 would be written as 0). With round_int = FALSE, terra's truncation towards zero is kept. Float data types are never rounded. A "FLT4S" file keeps about 7 significant digits.

  • No data: NA is written as terra's NoData value for the data type (for example 255 for "INT1U"). Values outside the data type's range are written as NoData, and terra warns.

  • Folders: filename's parent folder is created, with any missing parents, if it does not exist.

  • Checks first: before anything is written, filename must be a single, non-empty path whose parent is not an existing file, must not be a file x is read from (also with overwrite = TRUE), and must not exist with overwrite = FALSE.

This is the one writer constechr uses: write_rasters() writes each of its files with it, and align_raster() and extract_layers() write through it, so they all round, write NoData and decide data types the same way. Method choices are recorded in ADR 0014 and ADR 0027, and the rounding follows ADR 0010.

See also

write_rasters() to write one file per layer in a folder, or a multi-band file named after its source.

Other raster: align_raster(), polygonize_raster(), write_rasters()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# One layer, held in memory: the data type is inferred from its values,
# 1 and NA, as INT1U, with a message
pu <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, value = 1)
f <- write_raster_file(pu, file.path(tempdir(), "pu.tif"))
#> Writing /tmp/RtmpmUy3jO/pu.tif as "INT1U", inferred from its values (whole
#> numbers from 1 to 1), because the raster is held in memory, with no stored data
#> type.
#> ℹ Give `datatype` to choose another type.
terra::datatype(terra::rast(f))
#> [1] "INT1U"

# Or give the data type
write_raster_file(pu, f, datatype = "INT2S")
terra::datatype(terra::rast(f))
#> [1] "INT2S"

# A raster read from a file keeps its stored data type
write_raster_file(template, file.path(tempdir(), "copy", "template.tif"))

# Several layers as the bands of one file, each band named after its
# layer. cover has decimals, so with datatype = NULL the file would be
# FLT4S; as INT1U, 1.5 is rounded to 2.
x <- c(pu, pu * 1.5)
names(x) <- c("pu", "cover")
f <- write_raster_file(
  x, file.path(tempdir(), "bands.tif"),
  datatype = "INT1U"
)
names(terra::rast(f))
#> [1] "pu"    "cover"
terra::minmax(terra::rast(f))
#>     pu cover
#> min  1     2
#> max  1     2
